text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
German aircraft designer HUGO ECKENER was born in 1868. He circumnavigated the world in 1929 in the airship 'Graf Zeppelin'.

United States president HERBERT HOOVER was born in 1874. The American mining engineer, who was responsible for the Sons of Gwalia gold mine in Western Australia, founded the Broken Hill Zinc Corp before becoming president.

American singer PATTI AUSTIN was born in 1948. As a child she was promoted by DINAH WASHINGTON and SAMMY DAVIS JR. She released her first solo album in 1982 with the million dollar seller "Baby Come To Me" in a duet with JAMES INGRAM.
British singer LORRAINE SAMANTHA JEAN PEARSON with the band 5 Star was born in 1967.
**EVENTS**
1846 : The Smithsonian Institute for scientific research
was established in Washington.
1896 : The screw bottle top was patented at the Hope
Glass Works at Yorkshire in England.
1949 : The 'acid killer' JOHN GEORGE HAIGH was executed

in Wandsworth Prison. HAIGH confessed to nine murders after police found traces of one of his victims at his Sussex factory. The self-styled engineer had put the corpse in a drum filled with sulphuric acid. The victim was identified through her dentures.
1954 : Indonesia and Holland severed their last remaining
political ties.
1961 : Britain applied to join the European Economic
Community.
1964 : Rolling Stones lead singer MICK JAGGER was fined
$59 for driving a car in Liverpool without insurance.
1966 : The first American moon satellite, 'Orbiter One',
was launched.
1969 : Film actress SHARON TATE was found brutally

murdered at her Hollywood home. The bodies of four other people were found in the house, which TATE shared with her husband, director ROMAN POLANSKI. TATE was eight and a half months pregnant with the couple's first child. Four months later CHARLES MANSON, leader of a hippie commune called "The Family", and members of his sect were charged with the murders. MANSON is still serving his sentence for seven murders committed in the Beverley Hills area over two days.
1973 : Adelaide conservationist WARREN BONYTHON and

Melbourne artist CHARLES MCCUBBIN became the first white people to walk across the Simpson Desert. They trudged for 32 days, collecting plant and insect specimens which were to be detailed in their proposed book.
1983 : Pilots banned flights into Canberra in protest at
a tax on their superannuation, and rejection of their pay rise claim. Prime Minister BOB HAWKE said the pilots were "out of step with the community."
1984 : America's golden girl of athletics, MARY DECKER,

crashed out of the 3,000 metre Olympics final after tripping over the leg of barefoot runner ZOLA BUDD. South African BUDD was given British citizenship in order to represent Britain. BUDD was initially disqualified, but race officials overturned this ruling after studying footage of the race. They ruled that the accident was caused by DECKER's aggressive tactics.
1987 : Statistics revealed that the AIDS virus was
claiming lives at a rate of one person per day in Britain.
1989 : Hungary opened its border to the West, allowing
thousands of East Germans to leave in a mass exodus which led to the toppling of the Berlin Wall.
1993 : The body of former president Ferdinand Marcos was
laid to rest on Philippine soil, encased in a glass casket and put on display, four years after he died in exile in Hawaii.
1994 : Pope John Paul made an impassioned plea for peace
in the Balkans on his arrival in Croatia. The Pontiff was making the first papal visit to the region of former Yugoslavia.
1995 : NATO sent U.S. cruise missiles into action

against Bosnian Serb anti-aircraft sites in a campaign to make the Serbs remove their siege guns from Sarajevo. Tomahawk missiles from the USS Normandy in the Adriatic were sent flying more than 200 km (160 miles) over the mountains of Bosnia to slam radar and missile positions near the Serb stronghold of Banja Luka.
